ai.description: Tokay geckos reach 30–40 cm. They are slate-gray with bright orange or red spots and vertical pupils. They possess adhesive toe pads and emit a loud, distinctive "tokay" call.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Tokay Gecko is best distinguished by its large, robust body covered in distinct, bright orange or red spots against a bluish-grey background, unlike any other Indian gecko.
ai.habitat: The Tokay gecko inhabits tropical rainforests and humid lowland areas, frequently occupying tree hollows and rock crevices up to 1,200 meters in elevation.
ai.behavior: The Tokay gecko is primarily nocturnal and fiercely territorial, often emitting a loud, distinctive "to-kay" call to defend its home range from rivals.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Tokay gecko is oviparous, laying a clutch of one or two hard-shelled eggs glued to surfaces. Breeding typically occurs during the warmer monsoon months.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Tokay Gecko is found in Northeast India, including states like Assam and Manipur, inhabiting tropical forests from lowlands up to 1,200 meters in elevation.
